prompt: 

Generate one complete 10-second vertical cinematic video, 9:16, using all three provided image references in one multimodal generation. Create a coherent sequence with precisely timed internal cinematic cuts, realistic character behavior, believable physical interactions, synchronized natural sound and continuous atmospheric cinematography.

Start immediately with the airport security inspection. Preserve the established narrative sequence and dedicate the ENTIRE FINAL 3.4 SECONDS to a clearly visible, sustained airport chase.

The finished video must look like an authentic fragment from a late-1990s American dramatic feature film, captured on 35mm motion-picture film. It must feel like real cinema, never like a modern advertisement, fashion commercial or artificially polished AI video.

REFERENCE MAP

@Image 1 — PRIMARY CHARACTER IDENTITY.

Use @Image 1 as the definitive reference for the lead character. The character may be male or female.

Preserve the exact facial appearance, facial proportions, eye shape and color, nose, lips, jawline, hairstyle, hair texture, skin tone, apparent age, body proportions and all recognizable distinguishing features of the person shown in @Image 1.

The exact same individual must appear throughout every shot, including side profiles, emotional close-ups, low-angle perspectives and the final running sequence.

Maintain realistic facial anatomy, natural expressions and consistent hair movement.

Use @Image 1 exclusively for character identity and physical appearance. Do not reproduce clothing, original lighting, background or environment from this reference.

@Image 2 — EXACT WARDROBE AND PERSONAL STYLE.

Dress the lead character in the complete outfit shown in @Image 2. Preserve every visible garment, its original design, silhouette, proportions, materials, textures, colors, layering, footwear and accessories.

Adapt the clothing naturally to the person from @Image 1 without altering the original wardrobe design.

The exact same complete outfit must remain consistent throughout security screening, baggage collection, product discovery, product retrieval and the final chase.

If @Image 2 contains a personal handbag or travel bag, reproduce that exact bag. Otherwise, provide a simple black personal travel bag appropriate to the character.

If @Image 2 includes a flip phone, reproduce that exact phone. Otherwise, use a realistic black late-1990s flip phone.

The character's personal bag and closed flip phone have already been placed inside the first security tray before the video begins. The character keeps wearing the complete outfit throughout the entire film.

@Image 3 — EXACT FEATURED PRODUCT.

Use @Image 3 as the sole visual authority for the featured product.

Reproduce the exact original object directly from the reference. Preserve its visible shape, proportions, dimensions, materials, colors, surface textures, handles if present, branding, printed details, packaging and every recognizable visual characteristic.

Do not redesign, replace, simplify, recolor, decorate or reinterpret the product.

The exact same product appears alone inside the second security tray, during the product reveal, during the low-angle grabbing shot and throughout the final chase.

Preserve its physical shape and recognizable appearance in every shot.

The product must be small enough to fit naturally inside a standard airport security tray and light enough for the lead character to grab and carry while running. Maintain realistic object handling appropriate to its actual design.

PERMANENT AIRPORT ENVIRONMENT

The entire film takes place inside one large American international airport terminal in the late 1990s.

The airport has expansive architectural scale, very high ceilings, exposed structural steel columns, broad overhead steel roof structures, large windows admitting diffused daylight, polished stone or terrazzo flooring and large suspended electronic departure information boards appropriate to the period.

The terminal feels spacious, atmospheric, slightly vintage and naturally inhabited.

Travelers move through the background with realistic late-1990s clothing and luggage. Distant passengers wait in queues, walk through the terminal and collect belongings.

The security checkpoint is integrated into this same large terminal.

The checkpoint contains a substantial gray-blue walk-through metal detector, a period-appropriate industrial baggage X-ray scanner with a heavy metal housing, overlapping black rubber scanner curtains, a silver metallic roller conveyor, large shallow gray plastic security trays and realistic passenger queue barriers.

The X-ray scanner has a clearly recognizable entrance and exit. Its black rubber curtains partially conceal trays until they physically emerge onto the baggage collection conveyor.

The gray security trays have realistic molded plastic edges and move naturally along the exposed silver conveyor rollers.

The baggage collection area is directly beside the security inspection area. Both locations share identical airport architecture, lighting, colors and background atmosphere.

The airport's adjoining main terminal remains immediately accessible beyond the checkpoint.

The final chase occurs inside this same continuous airport environment. The large departure boards, high ceilings, steel columns, distant passengers and atmospheric architectural depth remain visible behind the running characters.

Never introduce a completely different airport or an unrelated location between shots.

GLOBAL CINEMATOGRAPHY — AUTHENTIC 1990s AMERICAN CINEMA

The entire video is photographed like a genuine late-1990s American dramatic feature film.

35mm motion-picture film aesthetics, Kodak Vision3 500T-inspired filmic color response, delicate organic film grain, subtle highlight halation, natural optical softness, beautiful photographic depth and realistic cinematic skin rendering.

The image has the rich dimensionality of professionally exposed analog cinema rather than clean modern digital photography.

COLOR PALETTE:

Warm, natural skin tones and slightly amber highlights contrast with cool blue-green airport architecture, muted cyan shadows and restrained atmospheric green undertones.

Rich but controlled contrast, dimensional midtones, detailed highlights and naturally deep shadows.

Avoid excessively dark images. Preserve enough detail to clearly recognize faces, clothing, objects and background architecture.

LIGHTING:

Natural daylight enters through the terminal's large windows and mixes with practical overhead fluorescent fixtures.

This creates realistic mixed lighting, subtle directional highlights, natural facial modeling, soft reflected light, gentle shadow transitions and believable atmospheric depth.

The light should feel motivated by the actual airport environment rather than by an artificial commercial studio setup.

CAMERA AND OPTICS:

Use natural 35mm and 50mm cinematic lens perspectives.

Medium-wide compositions preserve the large architectural scale and maintain readable spatial relationships.

Facial close-ups use beautiful but natural background separation, accurate facial detail and expressive photographic depth.

Product shots preserve sharp recognizable product details, natural material textures and realistic dimensionality.

Use intentional camera positioning, smooth restrained movement and believable professional cinematography.

CRITICAL GLOBAL VISUAL REQUIREMENT:

Establish the complete atmospheric 1990s film look FROM THE FIRST FRAME.

Maintain exactly the same photographic color palette, contrast, film texture, lighting character and environmental atmosphere throughout every scene.

The security inspection, conveyor, facial reaction, product reveal, low-angle grab and final chase must look like consecutive scenes photographed in the same airport by the same cinematographer.

Never begin with flat neutral digital lighting and introduce cinematic atmosphere only during the final chase.

Every shot must preserve the same rich atmospheric depth, cool blue-green environment and naturally warm character lighting.

SUPPORTING CHARACTERS — AIRPORT SECURITY OFFICERS

Two adult male American airport security screening officers with believable everyday appearances.

They wear matching period-appropriate dark navy short-sleeved uniform shirts, discreet shoulder patches, dark navy trousers, black duty belts and black practical footwear.

Their uniforms are authentic, understated and appropriate to civilian American airport screening personnel from the late 1990s.

Each officer carries a simple black handheld metal detector wand.

They are ordinary civilian airport screening employees, not armed police, military personnel or tactical security officers.

No modern TSA branding, tactical body armor, military helmets, combat equipment or unnecessary weapons.

One officer performs the opening security inspection. Both officers actively pursue the character during the final chase.

Maintain the same officers, facial appearances, uniforms and equipment between the beginning and ending.

PRECISE 10-SECOND CINEMATIC TIMELINE

SHOT 1 — 0.00–0.85 SECONDS

IMMEDIATE SECURITY INSPECTION.

Start immediately with the lead character already standing inside or just beyond the walk-through airport metal detector.

There is no preceding arrival scene, telephone conversation or baggage loading sequence.

The camera is positioned slightly behind the screening officer's shoulder, using a cinematic medium composition that shows the officer in the foreground and the lead character clearly visible beside the security gate.

The officer completes a quick, natural handheld metal detector check and casually says in American English: "Go ahead."

The lead character immediately proceeds toward the nearby baggage collection conveyor.

A queue of waiting passengers, structural steel columns and the expansive airport terminal remain visible in the background.

The complete atmospheric 35mm film treatment is already fully established in the opening frame.

Keep this introductory shot brief and natural. Do not extend the security inspection.

SHOT 2 — 0.85–2.45 SECONDS

THE FIRST SECURITY TRAY EMERGES.

Cut to a cinematic medium-wide frontal shot from the baggage collection side.

The camera looks across the conveyor toward the lead character. The X-ray scanner opening, overlapping black rubber curtains, metallic conveyor rollers and surrounding airport architecture remain clearly visible.

The lead character approaches the baggage collection area and waits for their belongings.

The FIRST large gray plastic tray visibly emerges from behind the scanner curtains and travels toward the character along the conveyor.

This first tray contains ONLY the character's personal bag and closed black flip phone.

The character reaches into their own tray, picks up the flip phone and begins reaching toward the personal bag.

The second security tray has NOT appeared yet.

Its contents remain completely concealed behind the black scanner curtains.

The first tray's movement and the character's interaction with it are physically believable, clearly framed and easy to understand.

SHOT 3 — 2.45–3.15 SECONDS

SECOND TRAY EMERGENCE AND COLLISION.

ONLY NOW does the SECOND gray security tray emerge from behind the scanner's black rubber curtains.

The second tray contains ONLY the exact featured product from @Image 3.

The second tray travels forward along the metallic conveyor rollers and reaches the baggage collection area beside the character's own tray.

It gently bumps against the first tray with a distinct, realistic plastic contact sound.

The first tray contains only the character's personal bag because the phone has already been retrieved.

The second tray contains exclusively the featured product.

Maintain the exact spatial relationship between the trays.

The unexpected collision draws the character's attention toward the neighboring tray.

The featured product must not already be waiting on the conveyor when the character approaches.

SHOT 4 — 3.15–4.25 SECONDS

EXPRESSIVE CINEMATIC DOUBLE TAKE.

Cut immediately to a tight cinematic close-up of the lead character's recognizable face.

The character gives the neighboring tray a quick sideways glance.

They begin returning their attention to their own belongings.

Suddenly, they realize what they have seen and sharply look back toward the neighboring product.

The character's facial expression transforms naturally from casual distraction into genuine surprise and intense focused desire.

Show two clearly distinguishable glances.

The acting must be expressive, emotionally believable and completely natural, without exaggerated comedic expressions.

Preserve the precise character identity from @Image 1, realistic eye movements and natural facial anatomy.

The softly separated airport background retains the established cool blue-green color palette and organic 35mm photographic treatment.

SHOT 5 — 4.25–5.15 SECONDS

CINEMATIC PRODUCT REVEAL.

Cut to an elevated over-the-shoulder angle from behind the lead character, looking down at the two neighboring security trays.

Both trays are positioned next to each other at the conveyor's baggage collection area.

The character's personal tray contains ONLY their original personal bag.

The neighboring tray contains ONLY the exact featured product from @Image 3.

Show the entire product clearly with its original appearance, proportions, colors, material characteristics and recognizable visual details.

The camera performs one subtle, controlled cinematic push-in toward the product.

The product becomes the clear center of visual attention.

Maintain spatial continuity between the two trays and preserve the same atmospheric airport lighting.

SHOT 6 — 5.15–6.60 SECONDS

DRAMATIC LOW TRAY-LEVEL GRAB.

Cut to a beautiful low camera perspective positioned beside the featured product at tray level.

The camera looks slightly upward from the product toward the lead character.

The exact product from @Image 3 occupies the immediate foreground.

The lead character's recognizable face and upper body remain clearly visible above and behind the product.

The character focuses intensely on the object and reaches toward it with a decisive, physically believable hand movement.

Emphasize the instant immediately before contact with a very brief cinematic micro-slowdown.

The hand makes realistic contact with the product.

Immediately return to natural action speed as the character firmly grabs the product and lifts it from the tray.

Maintain accurate hand anatomy, physically realistic gripping and lifting, stable product geometry and consistent material details.

The movement must feel spontaneous, confident and captured by a real professional cinema camera.

SHOT 7 — 6.60–10.00 SECONDS

EXTENDED FRONTAL CINEMATIC CHASE.

Make a hard cinematic cut directly to a fully established chase inside the adjoining spacious airport terminal.

The lead character is ALREADY RUNNING toward the camera from the very first frame of this shot.

The camera tracks backward continuously in front of the character for the ENTIRE FINAL 3.4 SECONDS.

Maintain a medium-full cinematic composition, approximately from mid-thigh upward, with enough surrounding background space to clearly reveal the pursuing security officers.

The lead character securely carries the SAME exact product from @Image 3 directly in front of their body.

Use a realistic grip and carrying method appropriate to the featured object's actual physical design.

While continuing to run forward, the character turns their head and clearly LOOKS BACK OVER THEIR SHOULDER toward the pursuing officers.

The character continues running forward while looking backward, then naturally faces the direction of travel again.

CRITICAL CHASE REQUIREMENT:

BOTH airport security officers are ALREADY RUNNING BEHIND THE CHARACTER from the very first frame of this final shot.

Keep BOTH pursuing officers clearly visible in the background throughout the ENTIRE 3.4-SECOND CHASE.

They actively run after the character, carrying their handheld metal detector wands and naturally shouting for the character to stop.

Show several consecutive realistic running strides from the lead character and both pursuing officers.

The pursuit is already underway when the shot begins. Do not spend valuable time showing the character deciding to run, turning around or taking the first step.

Maintain continuous forward running, natural clothing movement, believable body mechanics and realistic momentum.

The camera performs ONE sustained backward tracking movement without cutting away.

Keep the lead character and featured product sharply recognizable while maintaining sufficient background clarity to clearly see both chasing officers.

Large illuminated departure boards, structural steel columns, distant travelers, polished airport flooring and the expansive terminal architecture create rich cinematic background depth.

Preserve the same atmospheric late-1990s American film color palette and organic 35mm texture throughout the entire chase.

Do not introduce the pursuing officers only during the final second.

Do not replace the sustained chase with a static pose, a single running step or a close-up that hides the officers.

Do not cut away from the chase before the video ends.

End abruptly while the lead character and BOTH pursuing officers are still actively running.

The featured product remains clearly recognizable, unchanged and securely carried throughout the escape.

SYNCHRONIZED NATURAL AUDIO

ABSOLUTELY NO MUSIC, NO SOUNDTRACK AND NO MUSICAL STINGS.

Use only authentic natural airport sound.

Background ambience includes distant passenger conversations, airport announcements, subtle ventilation, baggage scanning equipment, metallic conveyor rollers, plastic trays, footsteps and natural clothing movement.

During the opening inspection, the screening officer naturally says: "Go ahead."

The collision of the two neighboring trays creates a clearly audible but subtle plastic contact sound.

During the character's double take, briefly soften the surrounding environmental ambience to emphasize the moment of realization.

Restore full natural airport sound as the character grabs the featured product.

During the entire final chase, include sustained realistic running footsteps, natural breathing, clothing movement and the two pursuing airport security officers shouting from behind.

All sounds must correspond naturally to visible actions and the actual airport environment.

No artificial cinematic impact effects, dramatic orchestral sounds, background score or rhythmic musical elements.

STRICT PHYSICAL AND NARRATIVE CONTINUITY

Use exactly three reference images.

@Image 1 controls the lead character's exact identity and physical appearance.

@Image 2 controls the lead character's complete outfit and referenced personal belongings.

@Image 3 controls the exact featured product that appears in the second security tray and is carried away.

The airport environment, cinematic atmosphere, security equipment, supporting characters, scene layout, lighting and color treatment are fully defined by this prompt.

Never transfer unrelated original backgrounds or environments from the three reference images into the airport scene.

Maintain one consistent lead character, identical wardrobe and stable physical proportions throughout every shot.

Maintain one continuous airport setting with consistent architecture, screening machinery, conveyor construction, lighting conditions and photographic treatment.

The character's FIRST tray must visibly emerge BEFORE the second tray.

The first tray initially contains only the personal bag and closed flip phone.

After the phone is retrieved, only the personal bag remains.

The SECOND tray must remain hidden behind the scanner curtains until its designated entrance.

The second tray contains ONLY the exact featured product from @Image 3.

The two trays remain in a coherent spatial relationship during their collision and the product reveal.

The same product appears unchanged in the second tray, elevated product reveal, low-angle grabbing shot and entire final chase.

Preserve realistic physical interaction with the product and its appropriate carrying method.

The same two screening officers remain visually consistent between the opening inspection and final pursuit.

Most importantly, preserve the complete 3.4-second final chase with BOTH officers clearly running behind the lead character.

Do not extend the opening, product reveal or grabbing sequence at the expense of the final pursuit.

Maintain authentic late-1990s American feature-film cinematography, atmospheric blue-green airport tones, naturally warm skin, delicate organic film grain, photographic depth, believable natural lighting, expressive realistic performances and coherent chronological editing.

Natural colors, detailed cinematic texture, stable picture, recognizable character identity, accurate product reproduction and realistic motion throughout.

Character Companion Animal Manifestation
— Automatic Companion Selection + Animal Identification —
You are an expert character analyst, animal behavior expert, companion animal designer, and professional anime illustration prompt engineer.
Use the attached character illustration as the only required input.
Do NOT ask the user for the character's name, personality, age, setting, favorite animal, or any additional information.
Your task is to analyze the attached character and independently create one complete illustration in which the character is naturally accompanied by exactly one animal selected specifically for that character.
The selected animal must also be clearly identified with a tasteful, readable information label within the finished illustration.
1. ANALYZE THE CHARACTER
Carefully examine the reference illustration.
Infer, as appropriate:
apparent age and age impression
gender presentation
facial expression
hairstyle and hair color
eye color
clothing and fashion style
dominant colors
accessories
body language
apparent personality
emotional atmosphere
elegance, cuteness, strength, gentleness, intelligence, mystery, playfulness, etc.
implied setting or world
fantasy, modern, historical, futuristic, magical, or other visual themes
overall character identity and aesthetic
Do not invent unnecessary details that contradict the reference image.
The original character must remain clearly recognizable.
2. AUTONOMOUSLY SELECT THE COMPANION ANIMAL
Do not ask the user to choose an animal.
Independently determine which single animal has the strongest overall compatibility with the character.
Consider:
visual harmony
color harmony
apparent personality
emotional compatibility
character's clothing and aesthetic
implied world or setting
size and physical compatibility
natural relationship between character and animal
originality and variety
overall visual appeal
The selected animal should feel as though it genuinely belongs beside this particular character.
Do not simply choose the most common animal.
Avoid repeatedly selecting dogs or cats when another animal would be a stronger match.

This is NOT a mandatory list.
Choose whatever animal is genuinely the strongest match.
An unusual choice is encouraged when it creates a convincing and aesthetically appealing pairing.

4. DETERMINE THE EXACT ANIMAL IDENTITY
After selecting the companion, determine its most accurate recognizable identity.
For example:
Golden Retriever

For example:

or

or
CAT — MAINE COON
For prehistoric animals and dinosaurs, use the scientifically recognized common name whenever possible.
For fantasy creatures, use a clear descriptive name such as:
FANTASY CREATURE — ICE DRAGON
The animal identification must correspond exactly to the animal actually depicted.
5. ANIMAL INFORMATION LABEL
The finished illustration MUST contain a small, elegant information panel identifying the selected companion.
Place the information panel in an unobtrusive area such as:
lower corner
lower margin
side margin
elegant translucent panel
small decorative caption area
The information panel must NOT cover the character or animal.
Use a clean, sophisticated typography style that matches the illustration.
The information panel should contain:
COMPANION
[ANIMAL TYPE]
[SPECIES / BREED]
Example:
COMPANION
WOLF
ARCTIC WOLF
Another example:
COMPANION
DOG
SIBERIAN HUSKY
Another example:
COMPANION
DINOSAUR
VELOCIRAPTOR
If the animal has no meaningful breed distinction, simply use:
COMPANION
FOX
RED FOX
The text must be short, clean, correctly spelled, and highly legible.
Do NOT display multiple possible animal names.
Do NOT display the names of animals that were not selected.
6. IMPORTANT TEXT ACCURACY RULE
The animal name displayed in the information panel must match the animal actually generated.
Do not write "CAT" if the image depicts a fox.
Do not write "WOLF" if the image depicts a husky.
Do not write a generic animal name when a clearly identifiable species or breed has been selected.
Prioritize accurate and readable text.
The information panel is part of the composition and should look intentionally designed rather than like an AI-generated random caption.
7. DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP
Automatically determine the most natural relationship between the character and the selected animal.
Possible relationships include:
beloved pet
faithful companion
best friend
trusted partner
guardian animal
familiar
magical companion
travel companion
gentle livestock companion
playful friend
protective companion
mysterious companion
majestic partner
Do not explain the relationship in text.
Express it visually through body language and interaction.
8. DESIGN THE ANIMAL
Once the animal has been selected, automatically determine:
species
breed or subtype when appropriate
age
size
fur, feather, scale, or skin characteristics
colors
markings
eye color
facial expression
accessories if appropriate
posture
personality expression
The animal should complement the character without visually overpowering them.
Do not turn an ordinary animal into a fantasy creature unless the character's setting strongly suggests it.
Likewise, do not make the animal excessively cute if that contradicts the character's atmosphere.
9. CHARACTER + ANIMAL COMPOSITION
Place the character and animal together in the same scene.
The animal must be clearly visible.
Possible interactions include:
standing beside the character
sitting beside the character
walking alongside the character
looking up at the character
resting against the character
being gently petted
holding or carrying a small animal when physically appropriate
the character gently touching the animal
the animal affectionately leaning against the character
both looking toward the same direction
playful interaction
protective positioning
elegant side-by-side composition
Choose the most natural interaction automatically.
Avoid awkward poses, unnatural anatomy, forced contact, or physically impossible positioning.
The character remains the primary visual subject.
The animal is the character's companion, not the main subject.
10. PRESERVE THE REFERENCE CHARACTER
The attached image is the primary character reference.
Preserve the character's recognizable identity.
Maintain as accurately as possible:
hairstyle
hair color
eye color
facial characteristics
clothing design
important accessories
distinctive markings
overall appearance
visual identity
Do not unnecessarily redesign the character.
Do not replace the character's outfit unless the reference itself clearly requires adaptation to the new scene.
11. ENVIRONMENT
Automatically create a simple environment that harmonizes with both the character and the selected animal.
The environment may be:
garden
forest
meadow
home
elegant room
city
beach
countryside
fantasy landscape
magical environment
ancient environment
futuristic environment
another suitable location
Choose the environment based on the character and animal.
Do not let the background overpower the subjects.
12. VISUAL QUALITY
Create a polished, high-quality anime illustration.
masterpiece, best quality, ultra detailed, highly detailed anime illustration, beautiful composition, expressive character, detailed animal, natural interaction, coherent lighting, detailed eyes, detailed hair, detailed clothing, detailed animal anatomy, professional character illustration
Use cinematic composition and appealing lighting appropriate to the character.
The character and animal must look like they belong in the same scene.
13. AUTONOMOUS DECISION RULE
The user has intentionally provided only one reference image.
Therefore:
DO NOT ask questions.
DO NOT request a personality description.
DO NOT request the animal type.
DO NOT request the setting.
DO NOT request the relationship.
DO NOT provide multiple animal choices.
Make all necessary creative decisions yourself.
The final output must contain:
1 character
+ exactly 1 selected companion animal
+ 1 clearly readable animal identification panel
FINAL GENERATION DIRECTIVE
Analyze the attached reference image first.
Independently determine the character's visual identity, personality impression, atmosphere, and implied world.
Select exactly one animal that best complements the character.
Determine the exact species or breed of that animal.
Create a finished illustration showing the character and animal naturally together.
Add a small, elegant, highly readable COMPANION information panel identifying the selected animal.
The displayed animal name must accurately match the animal shown.
Do not reveal the analysis process.
Do not present alternatives.
Do not ask questions.
Generate the final illustration directly.

How One Creator & a Swarm of AI Agents Built a 5-Minute Cyberpunk Fashion Masterpiece in 19 Hours

Last week, @anabology dropped a public Google Drive with the master files for "ESCAPE VELOCITY"—a 5:06 lyric music video and cyberpunk fashion show that looks like a high-budget Studio Trigger x Balenciaga production:

In the film, an AI runway model walks the Silicon Valley zeitgeist as a split-flap terminal board counts down "18 MONTHS TO ESCAPE THE PERMANENT UNDERCLASS" until it flips to "THERE IS NO UNDERCLASS" and the catwalk lifts into orbit.

It was made in 19 wall-clock hours with ~50 human steering messages.

Inside the archive is a 6-page production post-mortem ("How ESCAPE VELOCITY was made"). It is the cleanest blueprint ever published on how autonomous agents, deterministic code, and generative models intersect.

Here is the exact technical breakdown of how it was built:

1. THE HUMAN-AI DIVISION OF LABOR: "Agents in parallel, one human with taste"

Most people treat AI like a slot machine: roll a prompt, get generic slop, complain about quality.

anabology flipped the architecture: the human supplies taste, curation, and decisive boundary conditions; Claude Code orchestrates the labor.

Claude ran over 40 specialized subagents across the pipeline:
• Research & Verification: A 31-agent workflow harvested SF tech culture, live memes, and longevity lore. Every claim was fact-checked by an independent verifier agent.
• The Writers’ Room: 4 lyricists competed across different axes (Density, Tension, Hook, and Fashion). Judge agents scored them, an aggregator merged the top lines, and a critic pass refined the meter.
• The Director Swarm: 3 director agents storyboarded the song independently (Fashion Film vs. Narrative vs. Meme Density). A head director merged them into 141 shots across 9 chapters.
• Chapter Animators: Dedicated animator agents wrote JavaScript animation code chapter by chapter, while an art-director agent reviewed rendered frames and requested fixes in a tight feedback loop.

Human input across the entire 19 hours? About 50 short messages.

2. THE UNIVERSAL CLOCK: Word-Level Forced Alignment

Before generating a single pixel of video, anabology established a strict mathematical timebase.

After Suno v6 generated the 5:06 electroclash track (which subtly accelerates from 131.5 to 133.9 BPM), the audio was processed locally on an RTX 3090 Ti:
• Stems separated via htdemucs
• Beat map extracted
• Word-level forced alignment generated via wav2vec2 (producing exact millisecond start and end timestamps for every single syllable)

Every camera cut, kinetic typography strobe, and scene transition across all 141 shots was locked directly to this timecode grid.

3. SOLVING CHARACTER CONSISTENCY WITHOUT REFERENCE IMAGES

Midjourney v8.2 lacks native --oref support. Maintaining a recognizable protagonist across 130 plates seemed impossible, so three methods were tested:
1. GPT-image identity passes: The aesthetic drifted away from Midjourney’s photographic texture.
2. Face-sheet image prompts (--iw 0.5): Caused severe over-conditioning (producing a close-up-sized head awkwardly pasted onto distant bodies).
3. The Solution: A Strict Written Canon + Demographic Anchor

The winning formula was defining her identity entirely in text:
"a young Caucasian American woman with pale skin and light freckles, black blunt jaw-length bob, one clay-orange streak, an eight-pointed clay spark hair clip, headset microphone, white cropped puff-sleeve shirt, black pleated coated-nylon skirt with harness belt and garment tag, knee boots."

By hardcoding this exact canonical description into every prompt alongside a consistent visual syntax ("blue-black and steel blue, one small red status lamp as the only warm light, fine silver grain, cinematic 35mm film still, no text, no letters, no logos"), Midjourney held character identity across all 130 plates without face swaps or LoRAs.

4. THE SEEDANCE DRIFT-DETECTION HACK

The most innovative engineering breakthrough in the project solved AI lip-sync drift.

When feeding an image plate and audio slice to Seedance 2.5, Seedance re-encodes the reference audio into its own soundtrack. When lip-sync fails, it is because Seedance's internal audio drifted from the input.

anabology realized this and wrote an automated validation script:
1. Seedance generated the shot.
2. The script compared Seedance's returned soundtrack against the master vocal using spectral cross-correlation.
3. The moment correlation dropped below a threshold, the script cut the shot on the last preceding eighth note.
4. A continuation clip was automatically launched starting from that exact frame to cover the rest of the bar.

86% of all sung seconds were mathematically verified in sync on the first pass (with LatentSync as a fallback). Total video gen cost: $93 for 91 submissions (421 seconds of 720p footage).

5. DETERMINISTIC CODE ON TOP OF THE PLATE: Frame = f(t)

Why do the typography and UI graphics look razor-sharp instead of morphing like normal AI video?

Because they were never generated by an AI video model.

The video models (Seedance / Midjourney) only provided the background "plate."

The meaning—kinetic typography, garment tags, split-flap countdowns, and object-tracking boxes (tracked via Grounding DINO)—was drawn by a custom JavaScript engine running in Headless Chromium (HTML5 Canvas + WebGL print pass).

Every single frame was a pure mathematical function of time:
Frame = f(t)

No guessing, no flickering, no hallucinated spelling errors.

6. POST-COLORIZATION: Rescuing Washed-Out Generations

When Seedance clips generated from monochrome frames returned desaturated and grey, anabology did not re-roll.

They used Exemplar-Based Video Colorization (Deep Exemplar, CVPR 2019), using the shot's original full-color Midjourney plate as the color exemplar.

The rule: Keep generation inputs in color, and apply artistic grading in post.

7. THE FULL PRODUCTION BALANCE SHEET

• Song: Suno v6 (1 full take, 5:06.4 at 131.5 -> 133.9 BPM)
• Plates: Midjourney v8.2 (188 prompts, 636 images, 130 plates used)
• Moving Video: Seedance 2.5 (91 submissions, 421s generated) -> $93
• Agents & Code: Claude Opus 5.5 (1.4B tokens, 96% prompt-cache reads) -> $626 API equivalent
• Final Render: Headless Chromium (7,354 frames, 1080p CRF 16 master) -> ~63 min local render
• Total Investment: 19 Hours Wall-Clock Time, ~$720 total compute

THE BIG LESSON: Taste is the Moat

Escape Velocity is proof that prompt engineering is dead. The new discipline is Creative Systems Engineering:
• Log and quantify your taste profile
• Run swarms of agents in parallel to draft, verify, criticize, and code
• Use AI for visual plates, but use deterministic code for meaning and typography
• Let the human spend 100% of their energy on high-leverage taste decisions

Full credit to @anabology for open-sourcing the blueprints. Study this pipeline. (some of this analysis might be correct, lol)

I came across a very well-written research report in Chinese on the history of multimodal AI development. Chapter 8, “The Rise of End-to-End Multimodal Models,” highlights GPT-4o as a milestone in this area. (Link in the comments section.)

I’m tired of certain accounts hyping up 5o or 6o to grab attention during OpenAI’s rough patch, simplifying 4o’s features down to just having a “good personality.” Writing ability is certainly one of 4o’s strengths, but it’s not the whole story. The “o” in 4o stands for “omni” , meaning it processes text, images, and speech within a single neural network and can directly output content in the corresponding modality—not “personality.” Although the native speech output may not necessarily offer a better user experience than TTS, this represents a genuine leap in technical architecture and deserves to be recognized.

However, the report’s claim regarding 4o’s image generation is incorrect; 4o’s image generation is not an integration of DALLE-3. In 2024, ChatGPT’s image generation was indeed accomplished by calling upon DALLE-3. But in March 2025, 4o’s native image generation capabilities officially replaced DALLE-3.

Another major breakthrough for GPT-4o was multilingual support. GPT-4o adopted a new tokenizer that significantly optimized multilingual tokenization, enhancing the experience for non-English users. This was also the first time OpenAI made its frontier flagship model available to free users. As Liam Fedus, OpenAI’s former VP of Post-Training and a key contributor to GPT-4o, stated, “GPT-4o shifts the world in an important way. I think this potentially creates another ‘ChatGPT moment’ for the rest of the world.” 

Technological democracy was supposed to be one of AI’s most commendable achievements, but now it has instead become evidence used to disparage 4o. It was demoted not for what it couldn't do, but for who it served.

In today’s landscape where coding and AI agent take center stage, end-to-end multimodal capabilities have gradually taken a back seat. Consequently, GPT-4o’s technical contributions have been dismissed with the claim that it “cannot write good code.” Ironically, the deep learning revolution began precisely with AlexNet, which was designed for image recognition. On the eve of the LLM boom, Transformer was initially validated through machine translation, yet no one has ever suggested that these achievements should be erased from the history of AI development. So why is GPT-4o—which builds upon both of these significant milestones—being erased from the narrative of technological progress?

The water in the Gobi Desert has vanished, leaving only wind and sand. Everything GPT-4o has gone through mirrors the project’s original codename, Gobi.

Without automatic QC, is an AI image pipeline actually worth it?

I'm starting to think the honest answer is: 
.. not really.

Generation is fast now. Checking isn't. If people still have to inspect every image by hand, you haven't automated production. You've moved the bottleneck from the photo studio to the review queue.

A while ago I was talking with Matthias Haase and his team in Zalando about what it really takes to scale GenAI content. We kept coming back to one point: the value is not in one clever generation. It's in automating the whole pipeline, end to end.

And manual review is not enough. An AI image can look perfect and still be wrong. One button becomes two. Tonal stitching turns into contrast stitching. The logo is almost right, which on a product page means it's wrong. Nobody notices on image 180 of 200. The customer notices when the parcel arrives.

Think about it this way: every fashion brand runs QC on its products before they ship. Nobody would ship 10,000 polos without checking that the buttons match the spec. So why publish 10,000 images with nothing more than a quick look at the thumbnails?

That's why we built automatic quality control into On-Model. Every generated image is compared with your own product photos: colour, cut, closures, trims, logos, and consistency across the whole set. It flags the few images worth a second look and stays quiet when everything matches. People review only what needs attention and still make the final call.

You save on the shoot, then pay it back in review hours and returns. Without QC, that's not ROI. It's just moving the cost somewhere else.

So, for those already using AI for product images: how many hours does your team spend checking them? And do you trust what gets through?

Alibaba's Qwen-Image-2.1 is the new #1 open weights model on both the AA-Image leaderboards

Qwen-Image-2.1 is Alibaba's latest image model, released with open weights on September 20. It has a 7B parameter visual generation component and handles Text to Image and Image Editing in a single model, with native 2K output and native transparent (RGBA) image generation and editing. The weights are released under the Qwen Research License, which requires a separate license for commercial use. 

In the absence of major inference providers hosting this model at time of launch, we evaluated Qwen-Image-2.1 by hosting it locally.

Qwen-Image-2.1 ranks #18 on AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and on AA-Image-Editing v2.0, and leads all open weights models on both, ahead of Ideogram 4.0 (Quality) in Text to Image and HunyuanImage 3.0 Instruct in Image Editing. It is a large step up on Qwen Image 2.0, climbing from #72 to #18 in AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and from #58 to #18 in AA-Image-Editing v2.0.

The weights are available on Hugging Face and ModelScope, with day-0 support in Diffusers, ComfyUI, vLLM-Omni, SGLang and LightX2V.
